certificate: Associate in Science Degree, Neurodiagnostic Technology
program_description: Neurodiagnostic Technology is an allied health specialty for diagnosing patients with neurological disorders such as epilepsy, stroke, coma, multiple sclerosis, and many others. A competent Neurodiagnostic technologist has knowledge of the nervous system and knows how to properly operate many types of sophisticated instruments. Orange Coast College's Neurodiagnostic Technologist program provides theory and clinical experience in Electroencephalography (EEG) and in Evoked Potential (BAEP, PVEP, SSEP) testing as well as an introduction to other neurological testing procedures: Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS), Long-term Monitoring (LTM) for Epilepsy, Intraoperative Neurophysiological Monitoring (IONM), and Transcranial Doppler (TCD) Studies. The program is accredited by CAAHEP and meets the eligibility requirements for the EEG and EP exams of ABRET. It is completed in approximately 22 months (4 semesters and 1 summer); a new group of students begins in the fall semester of even years.
program_outcomes: To prepare the student for entry-level employment in the Neurodiagnostic field in the knowledge (cognitive), skills (psychomotor), and behavior (affective) learning domains as professional and competent Neurodiagnostic Technologists.
